Mixed Connective Tissue Disease: F10: Negative tests for anti–Scl-70, which can be present in some cases of Mixed Connective Tissue Disease, but not all
F8: Pulmonary function testing within normal limits, which might not be expected in advanced cases of Mixed Connective Tissue Disease with significant pulmonary involvement
F2: Chief complaint includes polyarthritis and joint swelling, which can be associated with Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
F9: Elevated antinuclear antibody titer of 1:320, which is common in Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
F12: Presence of Raynaud’s phenomenon, a common feature of Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
F11: Joint effusion, which is consistent with the arthritis seen in Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
